The hidden cost of legacy ticketing


## Your venue ticketing software should be  your biggest growth asset. Most aren’t.

Legacy systems were built for their business model, not yours. They obscure your data, take a cut of every sale, and own your fan relationships.

### No visibility into what drives revenue

Without real-time unified data across ticketing, merch, and membership, revenue optimization is guesswork. You cannot price what you cannot see.

### Data is siloed and inaccessible

Your CRM does not know who attended last Tuesday. Your marketing team cannot reach last season's buyers. The data exists, but you cannot use it.

### Fees erode every transaction

Service fees, per-ticket cuts, processing markups. Legacy platforms monetize your audience at every step and make fans blame your brand for the friction. Most also lock you into one fee structure, with no say over who absorbs the cost.

### Locked into rigid, outdated systems

Built on monolithic code, legacy platforms cannot adapt to your workflows. You bend your operations to the software — not the other way around.

### Your audience belongs to someone else

When a fan buys through a marketplace, they become that platform's customer. You get a transaction record. They keep the relationship.

### **Your brand takes a back seat**

While a fan buys a ticket to your event, they're also looking at the marketplace's logo, navigation, and often ads for other events on the same page. The marketing dollars you spent to drive that traffic end up reinforcing someone else's brand at the exact moment fans should be immersed in yours.

### Sports & Athletics

From professional leagues to collegiate programs, sports organizations demand ticketing that handles on-sale spikes, manages season packages, and converts game-day excitement into year-round loyalty. When that connection breaks, the cost shows up on the retention side: a fan whose scan, concession, and renewal history never reaches your CRM is a fan your marketing team has to re-identify and re-acquire next season, instead of simply renewing them.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about our venue ticketing software

### **What is Momentus Ticketing?**

**Momentus Ticketing** is the high-performance ticketing platform built into Momentus — purpose-built for venue operators, not marketplaces. It gives you white-label checkout under your brand, full ownership of fan and revenue data, real-time inventory and CRM sync with Momentus, and modern API-first infrastructure designed for high-volume on-sales.

### **How hard is it to switch from our current ticketing provider?**

Easier than you'd expect. Our migration team has moved venues from every major legacy platform with zero downtime to live ticketing. We handle inventory mapping, customer record migration, season ticket holder transfers, and historical sales data. Most venues are up and selling on **Momentus Ticketing** within 4–6 weeks, often faster for single-venue operators. For stadiums and arenas, that typically breaks into four phases: a data and inventory audit, season ticket and CRM record migration, integration testing across gate scanning and concessions, and staff training before the first event, all run with a dedicated implementation manager.

### **Who owns the customer data?**

You do — fully. Every fan record, every email address, every transaction history is yours and exportable at any time. Unlike marketplace ticketing platforms, Momentus never sits between you and your audience or markets to your fans on behalf of competing events. That ownership runs on PCI DSS-compliant infrastructure, so it comes with enterprise-grade security, not just an export button.

### **How does Momentus Ticketing connect with the rest of Momentus?**

Natively. Inventory, holds, and event setup sync in real time with Momentus event management. Ticket revenue flows into Momentus Payments and finance modules. Customer profiles unify with the Momentus CRM, so the box office, sales team, and event manager all see the same source of truth — no duct tape, no exports, no nightly batch jobs. For stadiums and arenas, that means gate scans and season renewals write to those same records the moment they happen, not after a nightly batch job.

### **Can it handle major on-sales and high-traffic events?**

Yes. The infrastructure has powered on-sales for global tours and stadium events with hundreds of thousands of concurrent users. Our queue system, edge-distributed checkout, and elastic scaling handle peaks that bring legacy platforms down — without requiring you to lift a finger on infrastructure. Mobile and QR scanning keeps gate lines moving even during a same-day sellout.

### **Will the checkout look like our brand or theirs?**

Yours, fully. Every checkout, confirmation email, and ticket wallet card is white-labeled to your venue. No third-party branding, no marketplace logos, no upsells for events you don't run. Fans buy from you the entire way through.

### **How does pricing work?**

Transparent and built around your volume. **Momentus Ticketing** is available to Momentus Enterprise and Elite customers as part of the platform — your account manager will walk you through the commercial model based on your venue type, ticket volume, and the modules you turn on. No surprise per-ticket fees on the back end. You also control whether service fees are absorbed by the venue or passed to the buyer.

### **What kind of support do we get during and after launch?**

A dedicated implementation manager guides migration and go-live. After launch, you get a named customer success manager, 24/7 ticketing operations support during on-sales, and direct access to the product team — not a help-desk ticket queue. Our box office support team has run on-sales for some of the world's biggest tours.
